questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Previous Students recommend this housing for international students 777 Broadway
https://www.icboulder.org/contact-housing
It is a dorm kinda experience sharing a room with 1-3 people, but it only cost 500$ a month. I decided to share room with someone also coming from KU, which made the experience more pleasant. It is close to campus, convience store and night life. Dont think you will get any more value for money than this

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Only freshmans were living on campus i.e 18 yo, so would recommend off campus.

The hill is where all the frats are living, Pearl street is the night life. So anything west or north from campus would be ideal. If you like going out i would recommend living walking or biking distance to Pearl street and campus. Although a uber is only 10-15$ at night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get a link to a portal where you can apply for courses. I found the timeslots af bit difficult to navigate, so i ended getting an alert on overlapping courses. You get access after the ordinary registration round, so the courses might already be filled.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were quick to answer emails

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all of them

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it as soons as registration opens, so you maximize the chance to get the course you want

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Not really the highest level, everything was kinda easy, got all A's without really trying. but i didnt really learn anything... 
All my courses were 3000-4000 range and really easy, i would recommend doing a combination of 5000+ courses you wanna learn something in, and then do a couple of easier courses to just pass. If a course both have grad level and undergrad in the same course, the lecturerers are the same, the grad level just have more workload

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Your grade often consist of:
- Attendance (my courses did not have attendence i suspect only 1000-2000 courses have, but havent confirmed it)
- Assignments
- Exams
All my courses i just took the assignments serious and got a passing grade, so i did not have to study for finals, would recommend tryharding assignments and then chill later in the course

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- CSCI 4113 Linux System Administration
- CSCI 4253 Datacenter Scale Computing - Methods, Systems and Techniques
- Introduction to Cyber security
- Introduction to Robotics

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Linux and datacenter were the best and most usefull, very hands on assignments. Linux lecturers were good, but i did not attend datacenter lecturer

Introduction to cyber security was a joke, hands on the worst structured course ever. But really really really easy, the most difficult part was finding out when you have exams and when assignments are due.

Introduction to robotics could be done 100% virtual although it did have lecturerers in person, but everything were recorded. If you just want a passable course this is the one, it does require workload, but it is mostly fun programming a robot and the exam is multiple choice at home you can retake 2 times

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Skiing started late october, got descent around december. Would recommend renting a car and going to A basin, Winter park and Copper mountain as they are way better than Eldora, a free bus does take you to eldora which is why it is good. I got 25 days of skiing during my stay

I joined the Triathlon team during my stay, it was fun training with other people and went to a couple of their parties. They have tons of social club, so find one for something you like to do, and meet people through that, you are not going to talk to people in classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Night life was pretty fun except everything closed at 2.
Would recommend The sundown saloon for cheap beers and always packed with students think barskowski, but with 9 pool tables and 9$ pitchers
The pearl street pub for good night snacks and cheap drinks
Rosetta and Spotted James for more night club vibes. 
Press play Boulders svar på ethvert sted på Gothersgade, Trashy men du skal nok få en hyggelig aften

Learn to play pool and play strangers, it were a great way to meet people and talking with them

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Skiing, Rocky Mountains national park is always great have been there before, so did only go 1 time during my stay in the winter with 30 cm of snow on the trails which were really fun. Hike the flat irons in all seasons view of boulder changes a lot. Boulder Sports recycle is a secondhand store with a lot of cheap patagonia, north face and arc'terix. In general just say yes to every opportunity, meet a guy who says he is going bouldering? ask if you can join. Someone going to a watch party for football, ask if you can go? Americans love foreigners (or at least people from Europe) and are very friendly.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: see other answers

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: If you think people in Denmark are woke, you wait to you see Boulder :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: All Americans are really friendly and talkative

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 4 months go by really quick. Boulder is expensive, i spent around 100k DKK all in all. It can be done a lot cheaper but also a lot more expensive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: As they say 'You will never be the fittest person in the room' Boulder is were sporty and outdoor lifestyle, if i were doing it all over, i would spent more time researchinh running clubs, hiking groups, etc. etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing living in a foreign country was an extended period of time

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: After 2 months i started to get bored, Honey moon phase was over and it became normal life, but then skiing started and it became fun again.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
